title: Learn Python – Full Course for Beginners
subject: cs
desc: A beginner course covering variables, data types, loops, functions, files, classes and small projects in Python 3.
comments: Perfect starting point, very clear explanations.
Helped me land my first internship, thank you!
A bit slow in the middle sections.

title: The Python Tutorial (official)
subject: cs
desc: The official tutorial from python.org: control flow, data structures, modules, errors, classes and the standard library.
comments: Authoritative and accurate, the best reference once you know the basics.
Dense for absolute beginners.

title: Python Tutorial – W3Schools
subject: cs
desc: Short lessons with a "Try it yourself" editor covering syntax, strings, lists, dictionaries, functions and file handling.
comments: Easy to follow with lots of examples.
Too shallow for real projects but good for quick lookups.

title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
subject: cs
desc: Harvard's introduction to computer science: C, Python, SQL, algorithms, memory and web development, with graded problem sets.
comments: The best intro course anywhere. David Malan is brilliant.
Problem sets are hard but incredibly rewarding.
Changed my career, highly recommend.

title: Neural Networks
subject: cs
desc: How a network learns to recognise handwritten digits: gradient descent, backpropagation, and later chapters on transformers and attention.
comments: Clear and beautifully animated, backpropagation finally makes sense.
Really helpful before starting a deep learning course.
Chapter 4 got hard for me, I had to rewatch it twice.

title: Learn Machine Learning in 10 Minutes (No Math!)
subject: cs
desc: A fast overview of machine learning buzzwords with a copy-paste demo. Included in the sample set to show that views alone do not decide the ranking.
comments: Clickbait. Shallow and misleading, nothing about how models actually learn.
Some definitions are wrong and the code has errors.
Not useful at all, a waste of time.
Good energy, fun to watch.

title: A Visual Introduction to Machine Learning
subject: cs
desc: A scrolling, interactive essay that explains classification and decision trees using a housing dataset.
comments: Beautiful interactive explanation of decision trees.
Clear and intuitive, perfect for beginners.

title: Python Data Science Handbook
subject: cs
desc: NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib and Scikit-Learn explained through runnable notebooks, from arrays to machine learning models.
comments: Excellent practical guide to machine learning in Python.
Clear code examples, highly recommend.

title: Introduction to Algorithms (6.006) Lecture Notes
subject: cs
desc: Lecture notes, problem sets and solutions covering sorting, hashing, graphs, shortest paths and dynamic programming.
comments: Rigorous and well structured. The problem sets are excellent.
Hard but worth it, I recommend pairing it with the lecture videos.

title: Big-O Complexity Cheat Sheet
subject: cs
desc: A one-page chart of time and space complexity for common data structures and sorting algorithms, colour-coded from excellent to horrible.
comments: Useful for interview revision.
Great quick reference to print.

title: Database System Concepts – Slides & Notes
subject: cs
desc: Chapter slides for the classic DBMS textbook: relational model, SQL, normalisation, indexing, transactions and concurrency control.
comments: Exactly what I needed for my DBMS exam. Clear diagrams.
Good notes, though some slides are text heavy.

title: SQL Tutorial
subject: cs
desc: Short, runnable examples for SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY and database design, with an in-browser editor.
comments: Easy to follow with good examples.
Too basic once you need window functions.

title: Java Tutorials: Object-Oriented Programming Concepts
subject: cs
desc: Objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces and packages explained with Java examples from the official Java Tutorials.
comments: Clear explanation of inheritance and interfaces.
A bit dated, but the concepts are still accurate.

title: Learn Web Development
subject: cs
desc: A structured curriculum from Mozilla: HTML, CSS layout, JavaScript, accessibility and frameworks, with assessments.
comments: The most accurate web docs anywhere. Excellent.
Great structure for self-learners.

title: Responsive Web Design Certification
subject: cs
desc: Interactive, project-based lessons on HTML and CSS: flexbox, grid, accessibility and responsive layouts.
comments: Hands-on projects make it stick. Excellent.
Some steps are confusing but the forum helps.

title: Pro Git
subject: cs
desc: The free, complete book on Git: branching, rebasing, remotes, internals and team workflows.
comments: The definitive Git reference. Thorough and well written.
The chapter on internals is amazing.

title: Essence of Linear Algebra
subject: math
desc: A visual series that builds intuition for vectors, linear transformations, determinants and eigenvectors through animation.
comments: Finally understood eigenvectors after years of confusion. Brilliant animations.
The best intuition-first explanation of matrices I have seen.
Great, but you still need practice problems alongside it.

title: Calculus Volume 1
subject: math
desc: Peer-reviewed open textbook on limits, derivatives and integration with worked examples and exercises.
comments: Clear worked examples and free. Excellent for self-study.
Good textbook, the answer key helps a lot.

title: Essence of Calculus
subject: math
desc: A visual series that rediscovers derivatives, the chain rule, integrals and Taylor series from first principles.
comments: Beautiful and intuitive, I wish school taught calculus like this.
Really clear explanation of the chain rule.

title: Integral Calculus
subject: math
desc: Practice-driven unit on integration techniques, applications and series, with instant-feedback exercises.
comments: Practice exercises with hints are very helpful.
Good, but some videos are outdated.

title: Unit Circle Diagram
subject: math
desc: Labelled diagram of the unit circle showing angles in degrees and radians with sine and cosine coordinates.
comments: Saved me during my trig exam. Clear and useful.

title: Statistics and Probability
subject: math
desc: Full course on data analysis, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.
comments: Great structure and easy to understand.
I love the practice quizzes.

title: Probability theory
subject: math
desc: Formal treatment of probability: measure-theoretic foundations, random variables, convergence and limit theorems.
comments: Too abstract for beginners, confusing notation.
Good reference if you already know measure theory.

title: Crash Course Physics
subject: physics
desc: Fast-paced episodes from motion and Newton's laws to electricity, optics and quantum mechanics.
comments: Fun and engaging overview.
Too fast to really learn from, but great for revision.

title: University Physics Volume 1
subject: physics
desc: Calculus-based textbook covering mechanics, waves, sound and thermodynamics.
comments: Thorough and well illustrated.
Good problems and a helpful solutions manual.

title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics
subject: physics
desc: The complete three-volume lectures, free online, covering mechanics, electromagnetism and quantum mechanics in Feynman's own words.
comments: A timeless classic, brilliant insight on every page.
Hard going without a strong math background.

title: Electromagnetic Spectrum Chart
subject: physics
desc: Chart of radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma bands with wavelength and frequency scales.
comments: Clear and accurate, perfect for my class slides.

title: Quantum mechanics
subject: physics
desc: Overview of wave functions, the uncertainty principle, superposition, entanglement and interpretations.
comments: Good overview but confusing in places.
Excellent history section.

title: Biology 2e
subject: biology
desc: Open textbook for introductory biology: cells, genetics, evolution, ecology and human physiology.
comments: Clear diagrams and free. Excellent.
Great for AP Biology revision.

title: Crash Course Biology
subject: biology
desc: Episodes on DNA structure and replication, cell division, photosynthesis, evolution and ecosystems.
comments: Engaging and easy to understand.
Fast, but I really like the animations.

title: Photosynthesis
subject: biology
desc: Light-dependent reactions, the Calvin cycle and C4/CAM plants, with practice questions.
comments: Very clear explanation of the Calvin cycle.
Helpful practice questions.

title: Animal Cell Structure Diagram
subject: biology
desc: Labelled cross-section of a eukaryotic animal cell: nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi apparatus and membrane.
comments: Useful for labelling practice.
Good, but the label font is small.

title: Introduction to genetics
subject: biology
desc: Plain-language introduction to genes, DNA, inheritance, mutation and how traits pass between generations.
comments: Easy to read, a good starting point.

title: Chemistry 2e
subject: chemistry
desc: Introductory textbook on atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, thermochemistry and equilibrium.
comments: Clear and well organised.
Great end-of-chapter exercises.

title: Ptable: Interactive Periodic Table
subject: chemistry
desc: Interactive periodic table with properties, electron configurations, isotopes and compounds for every element.
comments: The best periodic table on the web. Amazing.
Super useful for homework.

title: Crash Course Chemistry
subject: chemistry
desc: Episodes on the nucleus, electrons, stoichiometry, gas laws, acids and bases, and organic chemistry.
comments: Entertaining, but too fast and some topics feel rushed.
Good overview for revision.
Confusing at times.

title: Organic Chemistry
subject: chemistry
desc: Structure, bonding, resonance, stereochemistry, and substitution and elimination reactions.
comments: Helpful walk-throughs of reaction mechanisms.
Hard topic, explained well.

title: Crash Course World History
subject: history
desc: Survey from the agricultural revolution through empires, revolutions and globalisation.
comments: Funny and informative, I love this series.
Good overview but simplifies a lot.

title: World War II
subject: history
desc: Comprehensive account of causes, major theatres, the Holocaust, home fronts and the war's aftermath, 1939–1945.
comments: Thorough and well sourced.
Very long but excellent.

title: Industrial Revolution Timeline
subject: history
desc: Timeline of key inventions and events from 1760 to 1840: steam power, textiles, railways and factories.
comments: Useful summary for my essay.

title: U.S. History
subject: history
desc: Survey textbook from pre-Columbian America through the 21st century, with primary-source features.
comments: Balanced and clear, great primary sources.

title: Principles of Economics 3e
subject: economics
desc: Micro and macro fundamentals: supply and demand, elasticity, market structures, GDP, inflation and policy.
comments: Clear with real-world examples. Great.

title: Supply and demand
subject: economics
desc: The core price-determination model: demand and supply curves, equilibrium, shifts and elasticity.
comments: Good diagrams, a bit dry.

title: Macroeconomics
subject: economics
desc: GDP, inflation, aggregate demand and supply, and monetary and fiscal policy, with practice exercises.
comments: Very helpful for my AP exam.
Clear explanations of monetary policy.

title: Crash Course Economics
subject: economics
desc: Episodes on markets, inflation, banking, trade, recessions and economic systems.
comments: Entertaining and useful.
Some episodes feel a bit biased.

title: Purdue OWL: Grammar
subject: language
desc: Concise guides to English grammar, punctuation, sentence clarity and academic citation styles.
comments: My go-to writing reference. Excellent.
Helpful citation guides.
